title: Unbounded direct-image comparison
statement:
Let $k$ be a finite or algebraically closed field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, and let $g:X	o Y$ be a finite-type morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the unbounded derived categories of ordinary module sheaves over the constant discrete ring $A$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and the comparison morphisms $
u_X,
u_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ the canonical comparison
$\alpha_K:
u_Y^*Rg_{\mathrm{ét},*}K\longrightarrow Rg_{\mathrm{proét},*}
u_X^*K$
is an isomorphism. Here $Rg_*$ is the total right derived direct image, computed on K-injective resolutions [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and $\alpha_K$ is the mate of
$g_{\mathrm{proét}}^*
u_Y^*Rg_{\mathrm{ét},*}K\cong
u_X^*g_{\mathrm{ét}}^*Rg_{\mathrm{ét},*}K	o
u_X^*K$
under the derived inverse-image/direct-image adjunction [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. The underived direct images are [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and the inverse images are [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The displayed inverse-image isomorphism is [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]; the last arrow is the étale derived counit.

proof.text: If $X$ is empty both sides are zero, and if $Y$ is empty then $X$ is empty. Hence assume both are nonempty and put $e_X=2\dim X+1\ge0$ and $e_Y=2\dim Y+1\ge0$. Cover $Y$ by affine opens and, over each affine open, use the affine ind-etale basis of [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis, lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. If the affine open is $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is a basis object, [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] writes $C=\varinjlim_i C_i$ with $C_i$ finitely presented etale $B$-algebras. Hence $V=\varprojlim_i\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ with affine transition maps; composing each etale map to $Y_0$ with the open immersion into $Y$ gives the presentations required by [det-pe-unbounded-classical-bounds]. We will prove that $H^mR\Gamma(V,\alpha_K)$ is invertible for every such object $V$ and every integer $m$; Steps 11–12 prove directly that this suffices. Derived sections here mean evaluation of a K-injective representative, by the right-derived-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], with existence of the required resolutions checked in Step 2.

source.place: Opening paragraph: affine pro-etale basis and all integer degrees

proof.text: Fix $m,V$ and an integer $N<m-e_X-e_Y-1$. In the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], use the truncation triangle $E=\tau_{<N}K\to K\xrightarrow{t}\tau_{\ge N}K\to E[1]$; thus $\mathcal H^q(E)=0$ for $q>N-1$. The small ringed-site module categories are Grothendieck by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]. They also have enough injective objects by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. The right-derived-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] therefore gives K-injective resolutions for every complex in these categories and computes total right derived functors by termwise application to those resolutions; it applies to the additive direct-image and sections functors used here. For inverse image we use the exact-functor factorization below, so this step requires only the right-derived clause of the cited node. The functors $Rg_*$ and $R\Gamma(V,-)$ carry this triangle to triangles by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. The exactness of $\nu^*$ in [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], together with [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], does the same for inverse image. Thus we may use the long exact sequences of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] for both sides of the comparison.

source.place: Truncation triangle and its derived images; triangulated functor details made explicit

proof.text: Since $\ell^rA=0$, every $A$-module sheaf $G$ has torsion underlying abelian sheaf. Part (3) of [det-pe-unbounded-classical-bounds] kills its abelian higher direct images above $e_X$. Clause (3) of [det-pbc-conventions-module-cohomology] identifies these with the underlying sheaves of $R^qg_{\mathrm{et},*}G$. A module sheaf whose underlying abelian sheaf is zero is zero. Therefore $R^qg_{\mathrm{et},*}G=0$ for $q>e_X$.

source.place: Source paragraph: transfer the sheaf bound to module higher direct images

proof.text: The module direct image is additive and left exact [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact], and its source has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-sf-finite-cd-derived-upper-bound] with the bound of Step 3 and $t=N-1$ to obtain $\mathcal H^q(Rg_{\mathrm{et},*}E)=0$ for $q>N-1+e_X$. Exact inverse image [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] commutes with the kernel/image quotient defining cohomology. Thus $L=\nu_Y^*Rg_{\mathrm{et},*}E$ has the same upper bound, and each cohomology sheaf is classical by [sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves].

source.place: Source paragraph: finite-cd bound followed by exact classical pullback

proof.text: For every classical $A$-module sheaf $H$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, [sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves] supplies an etale $A$-module sheaf $G$ with $H\cong\nu_Y^*G$. The underlying abelian sheaf of $G$ is killed by $\ell^r$. Part (1) of [det-pe-unbounded-classical-bounds], with $Y$ as source, gives $H^q(V_{\mathrm{proet}},H|_V)=0$ for $q>e_Y$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], this site and its ring $A_V$ are $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}/V$ and $A_Y|_V$. The module/abelian evaluation comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] on this localized ringed site converts the vanishing into vanishing of the module derived functors of evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_V$, computed by injective resolutions; its enough-injectives hypothesis is Step 2. An injective resolution is a bounded-below complex of injectives, hence K-injective by part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], so these groups are $H^qR\Gamma(Y_{\mathrm{proet}}/V,H|_V)$. Apply [lem-sfb-unbounded-sections-localization] to $H[0]$ to identify these groups with $H^qR\Gamma(V,H)$. This proves the classical-sheaf evaluation bound required by the truncation lemma.

source.place: Source paragraph: classical-sheaf bound on V and localized derived evaluation

proof.text: Apply part (1) of [det-pe-unbounded-classical-truncation] to $L$ from Step 4, using $b=N-1+e_X$ and the evaluation bound $e=e_Y$ of Step 5. It gives $H^qR\Gamma(V,L)=0$ for $q>N+e_X+e_Y$. Since $N<m-e_X-e_Y-1$, both $m$ and $m+1$ satisfy this inequality. These are the source-tail vanishings.

source.place: Source paragraph: apply the truncation estimate

proof.text: For any $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ choose a K-injective representative $I$. The exact adjoint pair $g^*\dashv g_*$ in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] show that $g_*I$ is K-injective (Stacks Tag 08BJ). Thus both $R\Gamma(V,Rg_*M)$ and $R\Gamma(X\times_YV,M)$ are computed by the same complex: the degreewise equality $(g_*I)(V)=I(X\times_YV)$ is the displayed direct-image formula of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The identifications are natural because the equality holds for every degree and every chain map. To read the latter as derived sections on $(X\times_YV)_{\mathrm{proet}}$, use the site and coefficient identifications in [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] and the derived-section comparison [lem-sfb-unbounded-sections-localization].

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; blueprint target paragraph, evaluation identity (localization: sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open)

proof.text: Put $M=\nu_X^*E$. By exactness [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] and the classical-sheaf equivalence [sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves], $M$ has classical cohomology vanishing above $N-1$. Put $W=X\times_YV$, an object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$; no affineness of $W$ is needed. Part (2) of [det-pe-unbounded-classical-bounds] gives the bound $e_X$ on $W$ for all classical sheaves, since all of their etale antecedents are killed by $\ell^r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, using enough injectives from Step 2, and the identification of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and its coefficients with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$ and the restriction of K-injective resolutions exactly as in Steps 5 and 7 [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization, lem-sfb-unbounded-sections-localization], with bounded-below injective resolutions K-injective by part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], this is the same bound for the derived module evaluation at $W$, so $W$ satisfies the hypothesis of [det-pe-unbounded-classical-truncation] with $e=e_X$. Part (1) of [det-pe-unbounded-classical-truncation], now with $b=N-1$, gives $H^qR\Gamma(W,M)=0$ for $q>N+e_X$. By Step 7 these are the groups $H^qR\Gamma(V,Rg_{\mathrm{proet},*}\nu_X^*E)$, so they vanish for $q=m,m+1$.

source.place: Target tail, using the fiber-product bound of part (2), not the affine bound of part (1)

proof.text: The map $g$ is quasi-compact by the finite-type definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A field has no ideals except zero and the unit ideal, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian; [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] applied to the structure map of $X$ makes $X$ locally Noetherian. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes intersections of affine opens of $X$ quasi-compact. For affine opens $U,U'\subset X$ mapping to the same affine open $T\subset Y$, the inverse image of $U\times_TU'$ under the relative diagonal is $U\cap U'$. These affine opens cover $X\times_YX$, so the relative diagonal is quasi-compact, which is quasi-separatedness of $g$ by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. The canonical comparison for the bounded-below object $\tau_{\ge N}K$ is consequently invertible by [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]. This theorem specifies the canonical transformation and compatibility with counits, so it applies to the mate $\alpha$ fixed in the item, not merely to some isomorphism of its source and target.

source.place: Conclusion: check qcqs hypotheses and invoke the canonical bounded-below comparison

proof.text: For $S(K)=\nu_Y^*Rg_{\mathrm{et},*}K$ and $T(K)=Rg_{\mathrm{proet},*}\nu_X^*K$, the exact segments supplied by [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] are $H^mR\Gamma(V,S(E))\to H^mR\Gamma(V,S(K))\to H^mR\Gamma(V,S(\tau_{\ge N}K))\to H^{m+1}R\Gamma(V,S(E))$, and the identical segment with $T$. Steps 6 and 8 kill both end groups, so each middle horizontal arrow is invertible. Naturality of the mate gives $T(t)\alpha_K=\alpha_{\tau_{\ge N}K}S(t)$. After applying $H^mR\Gamma(V,-)$ this expresses the map for $K$ as the inverse target horizontal arrow, followed by the invertible map of Step 9 and the source horizontal arrow. Hence $H^mR\Gamma(V,\alpha_K)$ is invertible for every $m,V$.

source.place: Conclusion: explicit naturality square and the two vanishing end terms of each exact sequence

proof.text: Finally choose K-injective representatives of the source and target of $\alpha_K$ and represent its morphism by a chain map, using the Hom bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. By the right-derived-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], with the Grothendieck hypotheses checked in Step 2, and preservation of K-injectives under restriction to a localized basis site [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], their evaluations compute the derived sections in Step 10. Regard either representative $I$ as a complex of module presheaves. Its degree-$m$ cohomology presheaf is $V\mapsto\ker d^m(V)/\operatorname{im}d^{m-1}(V)=H^mR\Gamma(V,QI)$. Exact module sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact] identifies its sheafification with $\ker d^m/\operatorname{im}d^{m-1}=\mathcal H^m(QI)$; this is precisely the calculation of Stacks Tag 0BKV and does not assert that evaluation of a cohomology sheaf equals cohomology of evaluation. The identification is functorial, because kernels, images and their quotient maps are functorial.

source.place: Tag 0BKV, lemma-sheafification-cohomology; explicit kernel/image proof and affine-basis sheaf detection

proof.text: Let $\varphi$ be the map between the cohomology presheaves in Step 11 induced by the chosen chain map. The map $\varphi$ is an isomorphism at every basis object $V$ of Step 1 by Step 10. Every object $W$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is covered by the $W\times_YY_0$ for affine opens $Y_0\subset Y$, and each of these by basis objects of $Y_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Hence the presheaf kernel and cokernel of $\varphi$, computed sectionwise, vanish on basis objects, so every section of them restricts to zero on a covering; their sheafifications are therefore zero (a section of the sheafification is locally the image of a section of the presheaf, and that image is locally zero, hence zero in the separated sheaf). Since sheafification is exact [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact], the kernel and cokernel of $\varphi^\#$ are zero, so $\varphi^\#$ is an isomorphism. Thus $\mathcal H^m(\alpha_K)$ is invertible for all $m$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] to conclude that $\alpha_K$ is invertible. This proves the detector promised in Step 1.

source.place: Tag 0BKV, lemma-sheafification-cohomology; explicit kernel/image proof and affine-basis sheaf detection
